question: What does 21 CFR 820.10 require?
answer_raw:
21 CFR 820.10 requires that a manufacturer subject to this part must document a quality management system that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485 (incorporated by reference, see § 820.7) and other applicable requirements of this part.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(a) requires that the manufacturer document a quality management system that complies with the requirements of ISO 13485 and other applicable requirements of this part.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(b) requires that the manufacturer comply with the other applicable regulatory requirements in this title, including, but not limited to, the listed ISO 13485 Clause.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(b)(1) requires that the manufacturer document a system to assign unique device identification to the medical device in accordance with the requirements of part 830 of this chapter.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(b)(2) requires that the manufacturer document procedures for traceability in accordance with the requirements of part 821 of this chapter, if applicable.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(b)(3) requires that the manufacturer notify the FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of part 803 of this chapter.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(b)(4) requires that advisory notices shall be handled in accordance with the requirements of part 806 of this chapter.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(c) requires that manufacturers of class II, class III, and those class I devices listed in paragraph (c)(1) of this section and table 1 to paragraph (c)(2) of this section must comply with the requirements in Design and Development, Clause 7.3 and its Subclauses in ISO 13485.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(c)(1) requires that devices automated with computer software must comply with the requirements in Design and Development, Clause 7.3.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(c)(2) requires that the devices listed in the following table must comply with the requirements in Design and Development, Clause 7.3.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(d) requires that devices that support or sustain life, the failure of which to perform when properly used in accordance with instructions for use provided in the labeling can be reasonably expected to result in a significant injury, must comply with the requirements in Traceability for Implantable Devices, Clause 7.5.9.2 in ISO 13485, in addition to all other applicable requirements in this part, as appropriate.  

[1]  

21 CFR 820.10(e) requires that failure to comply with any applicable requirement in this part renders a device adulterated under section 501(h) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Such a device, as well as any person responsible for the failure to comply, is subject to regulatory action.  

[1]

question: List all requirements under 21 CFR 820.10.
answer_raw:

- [2] (a) Document. Document a quality management system that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485 (incorporated by reference, see § 820.7) and other applicable requirements of this part; and  
- [3] (b) Applicable regulatory requirements. Comply, as appropriate, with the other applicable regulatory requirements in this title, including, but not limited to, the listed ISO 13485 Clause.  
- [4] (1) For Clause 7.5.8 in ISO 13485, Identification, the manufacturer must document a system to assign unique device identification to the medical device in accordance with the requirements of part 830 of this chapter.

- [6] (3) For Clause 8.2.3 in ISO 13485, Reporting to regulatory authorities, the manufacturer must notify FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of part 803 of this chapter.  
- [7] (4) For Clauses 7.2.3, 8.2.3, and 8.3.3, advisory notices shall be handled in accordance with the requirements of part 806 of this chapter.  
- [8] (c) Design and development. The class I devices are as follows:  
- [9] (1) Devices automated with computer software;  
- [10] (2) The devices listed in the following table:

question: What is Part 821?
answer_raw:
21 CFR 821.1(a) requires that the regulations in this part implement section 519(e) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, which provides that the Food and Drug Administration may require a manufacturer to adopt a method of tracking a class II or class III device if the device meets one of the three criteria and FDA issues an order to the manufacturer. A device that meets one of these criteria and is the subject of an FDA order must comply with this part and is referred to, in this part, as a “tracked device.”

21 CFR 821.20(a) requires that a manufacturer of any class II or class III device that fits within one of the three criteria within § 821.1(a) must track that device in accordance with this part, if FDA issues a tracking order to that manufacturer.

21 CFR 821.25(a) requires that a manufacturer of a tracked device shall adopt a method of tracking for each such type of device that it distributes that enables a manufacturer to provide FDA with the following information in writing for each tracked device distributed.

21 CFR 821.2(a) allows a manufacturer, importer, or distributor to seek an exemption or variance from one or more requirements of this part.

21 CFR 821.30(a) requires that a distributor, final distributor, or multiple distributor of any tracked device shall, upon purchasing or otherwise acquiring any interest in such a device, promptly provide the manufacturer tracking the device with the following information:

21 CFR 821.4 defines the importer of a tracked device as the manufacturer and requires them to comply with all requirements of this part applicable to manufacturers. Importers must keep all information required under this part in the United States.

21 CFR 821.50(a) requires that manufacturers, distributors, multiple distributors, and final distributors shall, upon the presentation by an FDA representative of official credentials and the issuance of Form FDA 482 at the initiation of an inspection of an establishment or person under section 704 of the act, make each record and all information required to be collected and maintained under this part and all records and information related to the events and persons identified in such records available to FDA personnel.
